audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gives Ziggs levels 1-3 and calls 4-5 and first item Skill; the mirror settled on Level 1 Skill, Levels 2-3 Maokai, and everything from Levels 4-5 onward Ziggs.
audit.why: Levels 2-3 are exactly when Maokai has Twisted Advance and Bramble Smash but Ziggs has not yet out-scaled Sap Magic's refund; from level 4 the range gap takes over for good.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped as one atomic group across both layers, ratings re-scaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Maokai cooldowns anywhere and no mention of Sap Magic's cooldown being reduced every time he casts or is struck by a spell.
audit.why: Ziggs' whole plan is spell chip, and every bomb that hits him speeds his own sustain back up — that is the reason the early stages are not free.
audit.corrected: Twisted Advance 14s / 525, Bramble Smash 7s / 600, Sapling Toss 18s / 1100 written into phases[0..3].why, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Sap Magic's reduction stated in phases[0].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability slots are mixed up in five places: Sapling Toss is called 'W' (it is E), and wants.foe[0] has 'W Sapling Toss' rooting him — Sapling Toss does not root, Twisted Advance does. whys[1] calls the root a 'skillshot' when Riot's text says he dashes to the target. Nothing mentions that he is untargetable through that dash.
audit.why: A Ziggs sidestepping a 'skillshot root' will be rooted anyway; and holding burst for a target who goes untargetable mid-dash wastes the rotation.
audit.corrected: Slots corrected in spikes[0], early, whys[1] and wants.foe[0]; the targeted dash and its untargetability stated in phases[1].why and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] already says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', but no stage text ties Grievous Wounds to a timing.
audit.why: missingInteractions needs-antiheal; Sap Magic refunds chip and speeds up whenever Ziggs' spells hit him.

edits.before: Q bombs out-range every melee tool in the game — chunk Maokai on every last-hit attempt, but respect early minion aggro.
edits.after: Sap Magic heals him whenever he casts or is struck by a spell — your bombs speed his own sustain, so farm rather than spam.

edits.before: W Satchel online — your disengage button. You can now take a greedy trade and blast yourself out of the answer.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1, dashes 525 and roots on arrival — and he is untargetable through it. Pre-empt it.

edits.before: Full kit: E minefield behind you makes you nearly unchaseable. Bounce Q off the wave so Maokai can't read the angle.
edits.after: Bramble Smash knocks back at 600 on 7s and Sapling Toss lands at 1100 — he can trade at range now, so hold your Satchel.

edits.before: Stack Manaflow and chip Maokai below 60% — that's the zone where R + jungle help executes. Track Twisted Advance (Root) before every step-up.
edits.after: Chip him below 60% while Sap Magic is down — buy Grievous Wounds first, or his passive refunds the poke you paid mana for and the lane resets.

edits.before: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance (Root): Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1: he dashes 525 and roots on arrival, untargetable the whole way — so step up only once it is spent.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root): matchup-defining — Point-and-click root — count its cooldown before stepping up. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Satchel has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1 — a targeted dash-root he is untargetable through, so count it before stepping up. - Bramble Smash is 7s at 600 and knocks back. - Sapling Toss reaches 1100 on 18s. - Satchel is for the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: Slow melee Maokai eats free level 1 Q poke.
edits.after: Level 1 Sap Magic heals him off your own casts.

edits.before: Level 2 you keep chipping while his only answer is a skillshot root.
edits.after: Level 2 his Twisted Advance dashes 525 and roots you on arrival.

edits.before: By 3 your kit spaces him and clears his saplings.
edits.after: By 3 his Q knockback plus W root out-trades your kit.

edits.before: Maokai is a short-range tank whose only poke is W Sapling Toss into a bush trap, so you out-range him hard; poke him off the wave with Bouncing Bomb and drop E Hexplosive Minefield on saplings to clear them before they detonate.
edits.after: Maokai is a short-range tank whose only ranged tool is E Sapling Toss at 1100, strongest in brush, so you out-range him; poke him off the wave with Bouncing Bomb and clear the saplings with your own E before they detonate.

edits.before: Maokai is a slow melee tank with only a single skillshot root to threaten you, so the early lane is a comfortable poke matchup. Sit at max Bouncing Bomb range, chip him whenever he steps up, and watch for W Sapling Toss saplings in the brush that he can detonate for a slow-and-root.
edits.after: Maokai is a slow melee tank whose reach is E Sapling Toss at 1100 and a 525 dash-root you cannot sidestep, so respect the early lane. Sit at max Bouncing Bomb range, chip him when he steps up, and watch the brush for saplings he detonates for a slow.

edits.before: Land W Sapling Toss to root and walk you down
edits.after: Land W Twisted Advance to root and walk you down

notes: The packet suspectName ('Hold Satchel Charge') is a false positive. Per the mirror I wrote no claim that Satchel Charge cancels Twisted Advance — Maokai is untargetable during that dash and neither kit resolves whether a knockback interrupts it; see questionsForUser. Packet shows 1 game at 100%, so the chart follows the mirror rather than the win rate. diff reads 'FAV' while diffRating is 5.5/10 and breakdown.difficulty says 'Even matchup' — flagged, not changed, since the chart now splits four stages to Ziggs and two to Maokai and the user may want the label re-derived after the flips land.
